set: PL-300: Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst practice – Applied Skills Set 1

questions.stem: A company stores monthly sales data in 24 CSV files in a single network folder. All files have the same column structure. You need to combine the files into one table in Power BI Desktop and include new monthly files during subsequent refreshes. Which connector should you use?
options: SQL Server connector
Folder connector
OData Feed connector
Excel Workbook connector
questions.explanation: The Folder connector can access multiple files in a directory and combine files that have a consistent structure. When new compatible CSV files are added to the folder, they can be included during refresh without manually importing each file.
questions.subtopic: Get or connect to data
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Prepare the data: Get or connect to data

questions.stem: A retailer maintains transaction data in an on-premises SQL Server database. A Power BI report must query the database when users interact with visuals, and transaction rows must not be imported into the Power BI semantic model. The SQL Server source is accessible through a configured gateway. Which storage mode should you select?
options: Import
DirectLake
DirectQuery
Live connection to a Power BI semantic model
questions.explanation: DirectQuery keeps the transaction data in the source database and sends queries to that source when report visuals require data. Import mode stores a copy in the semantic model, while DirectLake is designed for supported data in OneLake rather than direct querying of an on-premises SQL Server database.

questions.stem: You are examining an imported customer table in Power Query Editor. Before cleaning the table, you want to see the percentages of valid, error, and empty values displayed for each column. Which data profiling feature should you enable?
options: Column quality
Column distribution
Column profile
Query dependencies
questions.explanation: Column quality displays indicators and percentages for valid, error, and empty values in columns. Column distribution focuses on value frequencies and distinct or unique values, while Column profile provides more detailed statistics for a selected column.
questions.subtopic: Profile and clean the data
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Prepare the data: Profile and clean the data

questions.stem: A sales table contains the columns ProductID, January, February, and March. Each month column contains a sales amount. You need to transform the table so that it contains ProductID, Month, and SalesAmount, with a separate row for each product and month. Which Power Query transformation should you use?
options: Pivot the January, February, and March columns
Transpose the entire sales table
Group the rows by ProductID and month
Unpivot the January, February, and March columns
questions.explanation: Unpivot converts multiple columns into attribute-value rows. The month names become values in a Month column, and their corresponding sales figures become values in a SalesAmount column, making the data suitable for filtering and aggregation.
questions.subtopic: Transform and load the data
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Prepare the data: Transform and load the data

questions.stem: You have two Power Query tables named Sales2025 and Sales2026. Both contain the same columns: OrderID, OrderDate, ProductID, and Amount. You need to create one table containing all rows from both years, preserving the existing columns. Which operation should you use?
options: Merge the two queries using OrderID
Append the two queries into one table
Group the two queries by OrderDate
Transpose the two queries into columns
questions.explanation: Append combines tables vertically by adding rows from one query to another and aligning columns by name. Merge combines tables horizontally through matching keys, which is not appropriate when the requirement is to stack records from identically structured tables.
questions.subtopic: Transform and load the data
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Prepare the data: Transform and load the data

questions.stem: You have a Power Query query named StagingSales that connects to a database and performs common cleaning transformations. You need to create two loaded tables, DomesticSales and InternationalSales, using different filters applied after those common transformations. Future changes to StagingSales must flow into both tables, and StagingSales must not appear as a separate table in the semantic model. Which TWO actions should you perform? Choose TWO.
options: Create DomesticSales and InternationalSales as reference queries of StagingSales
Create DomesticSales and InternationalSales as independent duplicates of StagingSales
Disable Enable load for the StagingSales query
Disable Enable load for both final sales queries
questions.explanation: Reference queries depend on the original query, so changes to the common transformations in StagingSales flow into both downstream queries. Disabling load for StagingSales prevents its result from becoming a separate model table while allowing the referenced queries to load. Duplicating the query creates independent transformation logic instead.

questions.stem: A Power BI semantic model contains a Products table with exactly one row per ProductID and a Sales table with multiple transactions for each ProductID. You want users to filter sales by product attributes using a standard star schema. Which relationship configuration should you use?
options: Many-to-many cardinality with Both cross-filter direction
One-to-one cardinality with Single cross-filter direction
One-to-many cardinality with Both cross-filter direction
One-to-many cardinality with Single cross-filter direction from Products to Sales
questions.explanation: Products is a dimension table with unique product keys, while Sales is a fact table containing repeated product keys. A one-to-many relationship with single-direction filtering from Products to Sales supports the star schema and avoids unnecessary bidirectional filter propagation.
questions.subtopic: Design and implement a data model
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Model the data: Design and implement a data model

questions.stem: A Power BI model contains related Product, Region, Date, and Sales tables. The measure [Total Sales] is defined as SUM(Sales[Amount]). A report uses slicers from all three dimension tables. You need a measure that ignores every filter coming from the Product table but continues to respect Region and Date filters. Which DAX expression should you use?
options: CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS(Product))
CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS('Date'))
CALCULATE([Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS(Region))
CALCULATE([Total Sales], ALLSELECTED(Product))
questions.explanation: CALCULATE modifies the filter context used to evaluate a measure. REMOVEFILTERS(Product) removes filters originating from the entire Product table while preserving the existing Region and Date filters. ALLSELECTED does not simply remove every product filter because it can retain externally applied selections.
questions.subtopic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Model the data: Create model calculations by using DAX

questions.stem: A Sales table contains OrderDate and ShipDate columns. A Date table has an active relationship to Sales[OrderDate] and an inactive relationship to Sales[ShipDate]. You need to create a measure that calculates shipped sales using the inactive ShipDate relationship without changing the model's active relationship. Which DAX function should you use within CALCULATE?
options: CROSSFILTER
RELATED
USERELATIONSHIP
RELATEDTABLE
questions.explanation: USERELATIONSHIP instructs CALCULATE to use an existing relationship for a particular calculation, including a relationship that is inactive by default. This allows shipped sales to be evaluated by ShipDate while ordinary sales measures continue to use the active OrderDate relationship.
questions.subtopic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Model the data: Create model calculations by using DAX

questions.stem: A Sales table contains numeric Profit and Revenue columns, and Revenue is positive for every transaction. You need to display profit margin as total profit divided by total revenue, with the result recalculated correctly when users filter by product, region, or year. Which calculation should you create?
options: A calculated column dividing Profit by Revenue and then averaging the ratios
A measure using DIVIDE(SUM(Sales[Profit]), SUM(Sales[Revenue]))
A calculated table containing one fixed profit margin per product
A Power Query column dividing Profit by Revenue before importing the table
questions.explanation: A DAX measure evaluates within the current filter context, so the ratio of total profit to total revenue adjusts to report selections. Averaging transaction-level ratios can produce a different result because individual transactions may have different revenue amounts.
questions.subtopic: Create model calculations by using DAX
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Model the data: Create model calculations by using DAX

questions.stem: A financial model contains an AccountBalances table with daily account balance snapshots. Some dates have no snapshot, and the latest available snapshot must be used to represent the closing balance for any selected month. A report must show monthly closing balances rather than totals or averages of daily balances. Which calculation approach is appropriate?
options: Sum all daily account balances recorded within the selected month
Average all available daily balances within the selected month
Use the first recorded account balance within the selected month
Find the last date with a recorded balance in the selected month and evaluate the balance on that date
questions.explanation: Account balances are semi-additive measures: they can be aggregated across accounts but should not be summed across dates to calculate a closing balance. Finding the last date with recorded data and evaluating the balance on that date also handles months where the final calendar day has no snapshot.
questions.subtopic: Create model calculations by using DAX

questions.stem: An Import-mode Power BI semantic model contains 80 million sales transaction rows. Business users only analyze total sales by product and calendar month; transaction-level details, customer attributes, and individual transaction identifiers are not required. You need to reduce model size without losing any information needed for these reports. Which TWO changes should you make? Choose TWO.
options: Aggregate sales amounts by product and month in Power Query before loading
Keep transaction identifiers as distinct text values in the loaded fact table
Remove unused customer attributes and transaction-level detail columns from the loaded model
Enable bidirectional filtering on every relationship in the model
questions.explanation: Aggregating transactions to the granularity required for analysis substantially reduces the number of fact rows. Removing unused columns also decreases memory consumption and improves model efficiency, especially when the columns contain many distinct values. Bidirectional filtering does not solve excessive model size.
questions.subtopic: Optimize model performance
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Model the data: Optimize model performance

questions.stem: A sales manager wants to compare total revenue across 12 product categories in a Power BI report. Category names vary in length, and the main objective is to make differences in revenue easy to compare. Which visual should you use?
options: Pie chart
Clustered bar chart
Gauge visual
Scatter chart
questions.explanation: A clustered bar chart displays categories on a categorical axis and values as horizontal bars, making comparisons across numerous categories straightforward. Horizontal bars also provide space for longer category labels, while pie charts become harder to interpret when many categories are present.

questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Visualize and analyze the data: Create reports

questions.stem: A Power BI report has three pages: Revenue, Expenses, and Profitability. Each page contains visuals that use the same Date table. You want a Year slicer selection made on one page to automatically apply to all three pages, while allowing the slicer to remain visible on each page. Which feature should you configure?
options: Sync slicers
Edit interactions
Drillthrough filters
Visual-level filters
questions.explanation: Sync slicers allows a slicer's selected values to remain synchronized across specified report pages. You can independently configure whether the slicer is visible on each page while keeping its filtering behavior synchronized.
questions.subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Visualize and analyze the data: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling

questions.stem: A Power BI report contains a summary page with sales by customer and a separate Customer Details page showing individual orders. Users must be able to right-click a customer in the summary visual, navigate to the details page, and see only orders for that selected customer. What should you configure on the Customer Details page?
options: Apply a fixed page-level filter for one customer
Create a report page tooltip using CustomerID
Synchronize a customer slicer across both pages
Add CustomerID to the drillthrough filters
questions.explanation: Adding CustomerID to the drillthrough filters of the destination page enables context-sensitive navigation from a source visual. The selected customer's value is passed to the destination page, filtering the order details to that customer.
questions.subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Visualize and analyze the data: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling

questions.stem: A logistics dashboard contains a column chart displaying total shipping cost by region. When users hover over a region's column, they should see a compact breakdown of shipping cost by carrier and delivery method without navigating away from the dashboard's report page. Which Power BI feature should you use?
options: Create a drillthrough page containing carrier details
Create a report page tooltip with the required breakdown
Add a report bookmark that hides the main chart
Configure a page navigation button to show carrier details
questions.explanation: Report page tooltips allow a specially designed report page to appear when a user hovers over a compatible visual data point. The tooltip can contain multiple visuals that show the relevant breakdown within the hovered data context without requiring page navigation.
questions.subtopic: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Visualize and analyze the data: Enhance reports for usability and storytelling

questions.stem: A Power BI report includes a line chart showing daily website visits for the previous 12 months. The horizontal axis uses a continuous Date field, and the vertical axis shows the daily visit count. The marketing team wants Power BI to automatically identify unusually high or low observations relative to the historical pattern. Which feature should you use?
options: Add a constant reference line to the chart
Add a standard trend line to the chart
Enable anomaly detection on the line chart
Replace the line chart with a decomposition tree
questions.explanation: Power BI's anomaly detection feature can identify unexpected observations in time-series line charts and highlight them for investigation. A trend line or constant reference line provides a visual benchmark but does not automatically identify statistically unusual points.
questions.subtopic: Identify patterns and trends
questions.source: PL-300 study guide, Visualize and analyze the data: Identify patterns and trends

questions.stem: You publish a Power BI Import-mode semantic model that retrieves data from a SQL Server database hosted on a company's internal network. The database is not publicly accessible. You need the Power BI service to refresh the model automatically every morning. What should you configure to provide connectivity to the database?
options: An on-premises data gateway
A report page subscription
A Power BI deployment pipeline
A sensitivity label on the model
questions.explanation: An on-premises data gateway provides the Power BI service with a secure connection to supported data sources inside a private network. After configuring the gateway connection and credentials, scheduled refresh can retrieve current data without exposing the SQL Server database publicly.

questions.stem: An organization maintains several approved Power BI reports in a workspace. You need to distribute a curated collection to hundreds of employees, display different report collections to Finance and Operations users, and prevent those users from editing the workspace content. Which distribution approach is most appropriate?
options: Assign all employees the Contributor role in the workspace
Export all reports as PBIX files and distribute them
Publish the reports individually to each employee's workspace
Publish a Power BI workspace app with separate audiences
questions.explanation: A Power BI workspace app packages approved content for distribution to consumers without giving them workspace editing permissions. App audiences allow different groups to see curated collections of reports and dashboards while creators continue managing the underlying workspace content.

questions.stem: A company publishes an Import-mode Power BI semantic model containing sales data for five regions. Row-level security roles have already been defined in the semantic model using DAX filters that restrict sales rows by region. Regional managers must open and browse reports directly in the workspace and see only their authorized region's data. They must not have permission to edit the semantic model. Which TWO actions are necessary to enforce the defined RLS restrictions for these managers? Choose TWO.
options: Assign the managers the Member role in the workspace
Assign the managers the Viewer role in the workspace
Add the managers to their appropriate RLS roles in the Power BI service
Grant the managers Build permission on the semantic model
questions.explanation: RLS restrictions apply to users with the Viewer workspace role, but not to users with Admin, Member, or Contributor roles. After publishing the semantic model, authorized managers must also be assigned to the appropriate RLS roles in the Power BI service. Build permission is not required merely to view reports and does not replace RLS role membership.
